answer: One defence is a stake-weighted reputation bond: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit grows with the volume it wants to handle. A newcomer may wander through low-value tasks to build a record, but it cannot reach the zenith of high-value work until its bond and history match. Peers mirror the agent's past behaviour in a public ledger, so a single operator spawning many identities must fund every one of them, making a fake-identity flood cost more than the profit it could extract.
